13.1.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.1.text: No translation of this sloka is available.

13.1.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.1.text: This is not a sentence, so there is nothing to fix.

13.1.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.1.text: Swami Gambhirananda has not translated this verse. Many editions of the Bhagavad Gita do not contain this verse, including the commentary by Shankaracharya. If this verse is included, the total number of verses in the Bhagavad Gita is 701.

13.1.author: Swami Sivananda
13.1.text: Arjuna said, "I wish to learn about Nature and the Spirit, the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and that which ought to be known, O Kesava."

13.1.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.1.text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, who is God, what is Nature, what is Matter, and what is the Self? What is Wisdom, and what is worth knowing? I wish to have this explained."

13.2.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.2.text: The Bhagavat said, "O son of Kunti! This physical body is called the 'field' (decayer-cum-protector); He who sensitizes it—His knowers call Him properly the 'Field-sensitizer'.

13.2.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.2.text: The Lord said, "O Arjuna, this body is called the Field, Ksetra. Those who know the self call the one who knows it the Field-knower, Ksetrajna."

13.2.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.2.text: The Blessed Lord said, "O son of Kunti, this body is referred to as the 'field'. Those who are versed in this call him who is conscious of it the 'knower of the field'."

13.2.author: Swami Sivananda
13.2.text: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, this body is called the field; he who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who know them."

13.2.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.2.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: O Arjuna! The body of a person is the playground of the Self; and That which knows the activities of Matter, sages call the Self.

13.3.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.3.text: O descendant of Bharata! You should know Me to be the one who sensitizes the fields of all. The knowledge of the field and the one who sensitizes it—that knowledge is, in fact, the understanding of Me.

13.3.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.3.text: And know Me also as the Knower of all Fields, O Arjuna. In My view, the knowledge of the Field and its Knower is the true knowledge.

13.3.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.3.text: And, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, understand Me to be the 'Knower of the field' in all the fields. In My opinion, that is Knowledge which is the knowledge of the field and the knower of the field.

13.3.author: Swami Sivananda
13.3.text: Do thou also know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Arjuna. Knowledge of both the field and the knower of the field is considered by Me to be the knowledge.

13.3.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.3.text: I am the omniscient Self that abides in the realm of matter; knowledge of matter and of the all-knowing Self is wisdom.

13.4.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.4.text: What is that Field and what is its nature? Why does it undergo modifications, where does it come from, and what is its purpose? Who is the Field-sensitizer and what is His nature? Listen to all this from Me collectively.

13.4.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.4.text: Listen briefly from Me what the Field is, what it is like, what its modifications are, what purpose it serves, and what it is; as well as who the Self is and what its powers are.

13.4.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.4.text: Hear from Me in brief about all that, what that field is and how it is; what its changes are, and what causes what effect; and who He is, and what His powers are.

13.4.author: Swami Sivananda
13.4.text: Hear from Me in brief what the field is, of what nature it is, what its modifications are, whence it is, who He is, and what His powers are.

13.4.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.4.text: What is called Matter, of what it is composed, whence it came, and why it changes, what the Self is, and what its power - this I will now briefly set forth.

13.5.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.5.text: This has been sung many times by sages, and also has been clearly decided in the various Vedas in different contexts by means of their words that are suggestive of the Brahman (i.e. in the Upanishads) and are full of reasoning.

13.5.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.5.text: It has been sung by seers in various ways, in various distinctive hymns, and also in the well-reasoned and conclusive words of the Brahma-sutras.

13.5.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.5.text: It has been sung of in various ways by the Rsis, separately by the different branches of Vedic texts, and also by the rational and convincing sentences themselves which are indicative of and lead to Brahman.

13.5.author: Swami Sivananda
13.5.text: Sages have sung in many ways, with various distinctive chants and also with suggestive words indicative of the Absolute, full of reasoning and decisive.

13.5.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.5.text: Seers have sung of it in various ways, in many hymns and sacred Vedic songs, weighty in thought and convincing in their arguments.

13.6.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.6.text: The five great elements, egotism, the intellect, the unmanifest, and the ten organs and the five objects of the senses.

13.6.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.6.text: The great elements, the Ahankara, the Buddhi, the Avyakta, the ten senses, and the one, in addition, the five objects of the senses;

13.6.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.6.text: The great elements, egoism, intellect, and the Unmanifest itself; the ten organs and the one, and the five objects of the senses;

13.6.author: Swami Sivananda
13.6.text: The great elements, egoism, intellect, and also the Unmanifested Nature, the ten senses, and one mind, and the five objects of the senses.

13.6.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.6.text: The five great fundamentals—earth, fire, air, water, and ether—personality, intellect, the mysterious life force, the ten organs of perception and action, the mind, and the five domains of sensation—

13.7.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.7.text: The desire, the hatred, the pleasure, the pain, the aggregate, the sensibility, and the feeling of satisfaction (or self-find): This, together with its modifications, is collectively called 'the Field'.

13.7.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.7.text: Desire, hatred, pleasure, and pain, and the combination that constitutes the basis of consciousness—or the individual self—have been briefly described here, along with their modifications.

13.7.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.7.text: Desire, repulsion, happiness, sorrow, the aggregate (of body and organs), sentience, fortitude—this field, together with its modifications, has been spoken of briefly.

13.7.author: Swami Sivananda
13.7.text: Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate (body), intelligence, and fortitude—the field has thus been briefly described with its modifications.

13.7.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.7.text: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, sympathy, vitality, and the persistent clinging to life—these are, in brief, the constituents of changing matter.

13.8.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.8.text: Absence of pride, absence of hypocrisy, harmlessness, patience, uprightness, service to the preceptor, purity of mind and body, steadfastness, and self-control.

13.8.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.8.text: Modesty, absence of ostentation, non-injury, patience, sincerity, service to the preceptor, purity, firmness, and self-restraint;

13.8.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.8.text: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-injury, forbearance, sincerity, service to the teacher, cleanliness, steadiness, and control of the body and its organs;

13.8.author: Swami Sivananda
13.8.text: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-injury, forgiveness, uprightness, service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness, and self-control.

13.8.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.8.text: Humility, sincerity, harmlessness, forgiveness, rectitude, service to the Master, purity, steadfastness, and self-control;

13.9.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.9.text: Absence of desire for sense-objects, and also absence of egotism; pondering over the evils of birth, death, old age, sickness, and sorrow;

13.9.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.9.text: Absence of desire for sense-objects, and also absence of egotism, the recognition of evil in birth, death, old age, disease, and sorrow;

13.9.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.9.text: Non-attachment to objects of the senses, and also the absence of egotism; seeing the evil in birth, death, aging, diseases, and miseries;

13.9.author: Swami Sivananda
13.9.text: Indifference to the objects of the senses and also absence of egoism; perceiving the evil in birth, death, old age, sickness, and pain.

13.9.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.9.text: Renouncing the delights of the senses, being without pride, having a right understanding of the painful problem of birth and death, and of age and sickness;

13.10.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.10.text: Non-attachment, detachment towards one's children, wives, houses, and the like; and a constant even-mindedness in the occurrence of desirable and undesirable things.

13.10.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.10.text: Non-attachment, absence of clinging to son, wife, home, and the like, and constant even-mindedness in regard to all desirable and undesirable events;

13.10.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.10.text: Non-attachment and absence of fondness with regard to sons, wives, homes, etc., and constant equanimity of the mind with regard to the attainment of both the desirable and the undesirable;

13.10.author: Swami Sivananda
13.10.text: Non-attachment, non-identification of the Self with son, wife, home, and the rest, and constant even-mindedness in the face of the attainment of both desirable and undesirable.

13.10.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.10.text: Indifference, non-attachment to sex, progeny, or home, equanimity in both good fortune and bad;

13.11.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.11.text: And an unwavering devotion to Me, with the Yoga of non-duality; taking refuge in a solitary place; disinterest in a crowd of people;

13.11.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.11.text: Constantly devote yourself to Me alone, resort to solitary places, and dislike crowds.

13.11.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.11.text: And unwavering devotion to Me with single-minded concentration; inclination to retreat to a clean place; lack of delight in a crowd of people;

13.11.author: Swami Sivananda
13.11.text: Unswerving devotion to Me through the Yoga of non-separation, resorting to solitary places, and a distaste for the company of people.

13.11.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.11.text: Unswerving devotion to Me, with concentration on Me and Me alone, a love for solitude, and indifference to social life;

13.12.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.12.text: Constancy in Self-knowledge, and viewing things with the aim of knowing the Reality—all this is declared to be conducive to true knowledge, and what is opposed to this is conducive to wrong knowledge.

13.12.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.12.text: Constant contemplation on the knowledge pertaining to the self, reflection for the attainment of knowledge of the truth—this is declared to be knowledge, and what is contrary to it is ignorance.

13.12.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.12.text: Steadfastness in the knowledge of the Self, contemplation on the Goal of the knowledge of Reality—this is spoken of as Knowledge. Ignorance is that which is other than this.

13.12.author: Swami Sivananda
13.12.text: Constancy in Self-knowledge, the perception of the end of true knowledge—this is declared to be knowledge, and what is opposed to it is ignorance.

13.12.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.12.text: Constant yearning for the knowledge of the Self, and pondering over the lessons of the great Truth—this is wisdom; all else is ignorance.

13.13.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.13.text: I shall describe that which is to be known, by knowing which one attains freedom from death: the Supreme Brahman is beginningless and is said to be neither existent nor non-existent.

13.13.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.13.text: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains the immortal Self. It is beginningless Brahman, having Me as the Highest (Anadi Matparam); it is said to be neither being nor non-being.

13.13.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.13.text: I shall speak of that which is to be known, by realizing which one attains immortality. The supreme Brahman is without any beginning; that is called neither being nor non-being.

13.13.author: Swami Sivananda
13.13.text: I will declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality; the beginningless Supreme Brahman, which is neither being nor non-being.

13.13.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.13.text: I will now speak to you of that great truth which one ought to know, since by it one will attain immortal bliss—that which is without beginning, the eternal spirit which dwells in me, neither with form nor without it.

13.14.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.14.text: It has hands and feet of all, has eyes, heads, and faces of all, has ears of all in the world; It envelops all.

13.14.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.14.text: Its hands and feet are everywhere; Its eyes, heads, and mouths are everywhere; Its ears are on all sides; and It exists, encompassing all things.

13.14.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.14.text: That Knowable, which has hands and feet everywhere, which has eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere, which has ears everywhere, exists in creatures by pervading them all.

13.14.author: Swami Sivananda
13.14.text: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere, He exists in the worlds, enveloping all.

13.14.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.14.text: Everywhere are Its hands and feet; everywhere It has eyes that see, heads that think, and mouths that speak; everywhere It listens; It dwells in all the worlds and envelops them all.

13.15.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.15.text: It illuminates all the senses; yet it has no sense organs; it is unattached, yet supports all; it is free from the bonds, yet enjoys the bonds.

13.15.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.15.text: Shining by the functions of the senses, yet devoid of the senses, detached yet supporting all, devoid of the Gunas yet experiencing the Gunas;

13.15.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.15.text: Shining through the functions of all the organs, yet devoid of all the organs; unattached, and verily the supporter of all; without quality, and the perceiver of qualities.

13.15.author: Swami Sivananda
13.15.text: Shining by the functions of all the senses, yet without being attached to them; unattached, yet supporting all; devoid of qualities, yet the experiencer of them.

13.15.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.15.text: Beyond the senses, it yet shines through every sense perception; bound to nothing, it yet sustains everything; unaffected by the qualities, it still enjoys them all.

13.16.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.16.text: It is without and within every being, unmoving yet moving; due to its subtle nature, it is incomprehensible; it exists far away yet is near.

13.16.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.16.text: It is within and without all beings; It is unmoving yet moving; It is so subtle that none can comprehend it; It is far away yet very near.

13.16.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.16.text: Existing both outside and inside all beings, moving and non-moving, It is incomprehensible due to Its subtlety. It is far away, yet near.

13.16.author: Swami Sivananda
13.16.text: It is within and without all beings, both the unmoving and the moving; It is subtle and unknowable, and It is near and far away.

13.16.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.16.text: It is within all beings, yet outside; motionless yet moving; too subtle to be perceived; far away yet ever near.

13.17.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.17.text: It remains undistinguished among the distinguished beings, and appears as if distinguished. It is to be known as the supporter of beings, and also as their swallower and originator.

13.17.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.17.text: Undivided yet appearing as if divided among beings, this Self is to be known as the supporter of the elements. It devours them and causes their generation.

13.17.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.17.text: The Knowable, though undivided, appears to exist as divided in all beings, and It is the sustainer, devourer, and originator of all beings.

13.17.author: Swami Sivananda
13.17.text: Undivided yet, It exists as if divided in beings; It is to be known as the supporter of beings; It devours and It generates.

13.17.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.17.text: In all beings, undivided yet living in division, it is the upholder of all, both creator and destroyer alike.

13.18.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.18.text: This is the Light of all lights, stated to be beyond darkness; it is to be known by the above knowledge; it is to be attained only through knowledge; and it distinctly remains in the heart of all.

13.18.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.18.text: The light of all lights is said to be beyond Tamas (darkness); it is known to be knowledge, to be attained through knowledge, and to be present in the hearts of all.

13.18.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.18.text: That is the Light of all lights; It is spoken of as beyond darkness. It is Knowledge, the Knowable, and the Known. It is specially situated in the hearts of all.

13.18.author: Swami Sivananda
13.18.text: That Light of all lights is said to be beyond darkness: knowledge, the knowable, and the goal of knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.

13.18.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.18.text: It is the light of lights, beyond the reach of darkness; the wisdom, the only thing worth knowing or that wisdom can teach; the presence in the hearts of all.

13.19.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.19.text: This field, as well as the knowledge and what is to be known, are all mentioned collectively; clearly understanding this, My devotee becomes worthy of My state.

13.19.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.19.text: Thus, the Ksetra, knowledge, and the object of knowledge have been briefly set forth. On knowing this, My devotee becomes fit to attain My state.

13.19.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.19.text: Thus, in brief, the field, Knowledge, and the Knowable have been spoken of. By understanding this, My devotee becomes qualified for My state.

13.19.author: Swami Sivananda
13.19.text: Thus, the field, as well as knowledge and the knowable, have been briefly stated. My devotee, knowing this, enters into My being.

13.19.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.19.text: Thus, I have briefly told you what Matter is, the Self worth realizing, and what Wisdom is. He who is devoted to Me knows, and he will assuredly enter into Me.

13.20.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.20.text: Both the Material Cause and the Soul are beginningless; you should know this. You should also know that the modifications and strands are born from the Material Cause.

13.20.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.20.text: Know that both Prakṛti and the Self (Puruṣa) are without beginning; know that all modifications and the attributes are born from Prakṛti.

13.20.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.20.text: Know both Nature and the individual soul to be verily without beginning; know the modifications as well as the qualities to be born of Nature.

13.20.author: Swami Sivananda
13.20.text: Know that Nature (matter) and the Spirit are both beginningless, and know also that all modifications and qualities are born from Nature.

13.20.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.20.text: Know further that Nature and God have no beginning, and that differences in character and quality originate from Nature only.

13.21.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.21.text: In creating the process of cause and effect, the material cause is said to be the basis; and in experiencing pleasure and pain, the soul is said to be the basis.

13.21.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.21.text: The Prakṛti is said to be the cause of agency to the body (Kārya) and sense-organs (Karaṇa); the Self is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.

13.21.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.21.text: With regard to the source of the body and its organs, Nature is said to be the cause; the soul is the cause so far as the enjoyment of happiness and sorrow is concerned.

13.21.author: Swami Sivananda
13.21.text: In the production of the effect and the cause, Nature (matter) is said to be the cause; in the experience of pleasure and pain, the soul is said to be the one responsible.

13.21.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.21.text: Nature is the law that generates cause and effect; God is the source of all pleasure and pain.

13.22.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.22.text: For, the soul, seated on the material cause, enjoys the strands born of the material cause; His attachment to the strands is the cause of his births in good and evil wombs.

13.22.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.22.text: Indeed, the self seated in Prakrti experiences the Gunas born of Prakrti. Its attachment to these Gunas is the cause of birth in good and evil wombs.

13.22.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.22.text: Since the soul is seated in Nature, therefore it experiences the qualities born of Nature. Contact with the qualities is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.

13.22.author: Swami Sivananda
13.22.text: The soul seated in Nature experiences the qualities born of Nature; attachment to the qualities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.

13.22.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.22.text: God, dwelling in the heart of Nature, experiences the qualities that Nature brings forth; and His affinity towards these qualities is the reason for His living in a good or evil body.

13.23.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.23.text: The Supreme Soul in this corporeal body is called the Spectator, the Assenter, the Supporter, the Experiencer, the Mighty Lord, and also the Supreme Self.

13.23.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.23.text: The self in the body is called the spectator, approver, supporter, experiencer, great lord, and supreme self.

13.23.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.23.text: He who is the Witness, the Permitter, the Sustainer, the Experiencer, the great Lord, and who is also spoken of as the transcendental Self, is the supreme Person in this body.

13.23.author: Swami Sivananda
13.23.text: The Supreme Soul in this body is also called the observer, the permitter, the sustainer, the enjoyer, the great Lord, and the Supreme Self.

13.23.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.23.text: Thus, in the body of man dwells the Supreme God; He who sees, permits, upholds, and enjoys is the Highest God and the Highest Self.

13.24.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.24.text: He who knows, in this manner, the Soul and the Material Cause together with their strands—he is not reborn, even though he may act in various ways.

13.24.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.24.text: He who understands the Self and Prakriti, along with the Gunas, will not be born again, no matter what state he may be in.

13.24.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.24.text: He who knows thus the Person, Nature, and Qualities will not be born again, no matter how he may live.

13.24.author: Swami Sivananda
13.24.text: He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter together with their qualities, in whatever condition he may be, he is not reborn.

13.24.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.24.text: He who understands God and Nature, along with her qualities, whatever his condition in life may be, will not come back to earth.

13.25.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.25.text: However, some yogis perceive the Self as the Self within the self through meditation, others through knowledge-yoga, and still others through action-yoga.

13.25.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.25.text: Some perceive the Self within the self (body) through meditation of the mind, others through Sankhya Yoga, and still others through Karma Yoga.

13.25.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.25.text: Some realize the Self in their intellect through meditation, others through Sankhya-Yoga, and still others through Karma-Yoga, with the help of the internal organ.

13.25.author: Swami Sivananda
13.25.text: Some behold the Self within themselves through meditation, others through the Yoga of knowledge, and still others through the Yoga of action.

13.25.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.25.text: Some realize the Supreme by meditating, with its aid, on the Self within; others by pure reason; and still others by right action.

13.26.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.26.text: But others, who have no knowledge of this nature, listen from others and reflect [accordingly]; they too, being devoted to what they have heard, do cross over death.

13.26.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.26.text: But some, who do not know this, having heard from others, worship accordingly—these too, devoted to what they hear, pass beyond death.

13.26.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.26.text: Others, again, who do not know thus, take to thinking after hearing from others; they too, who are devoted to hearing, certainly overcome death.

13.26.author: Swami Sivananda
13.26.text: Others, too, who do not know thus, worship, having heard of It from others; they, too, cross beyond death, regarding what they have heard as the supreme refuge.

13.26.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.26.text: Others, again, having no direct knowledge but only hearing from others, still worship, and, if they are true to the teachings, they too will cross the sea of death.

13.27.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.27.text: Whatever living being is born, stationary or moving, you should know that all this has a close connection with the Field and the Field-sensitizer, O best of the Bharatas!

13.27.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.27.text: Whatever being is born, whether it be moving or stationary, know, O Arjuna, that it is through the combination of the Ksetra (body) and Ksetrajna (knower of the Field).

13.27.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.27.text: O scion of the Bharata dynasty, whatever object, moving or non-moving, comes into existence, know that to be from the combination of the field and the Knower of the field!

13.27.author: Swami Sivananda
13.27.text: Wherever a being is born, whether unmoving or moving, know thou, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), that it is from the union of the field and its knower.

13.27.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.27.text: Wherever life is seen in things movable or immovable, it is the result of the combination of Matter and Spirit.

13.28.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.28.text: Whoever perceives the Supreme Lord as abiding and non-perishing in all beings, even as they perish, perceives properly.

13.28.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.28.text: Who sees the supreme ruler dwelling alike in all bodies and never perishing, even when they perish, he indeed sees.

13.28.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.28.text: He who sees the Supreme Lord existing truly in all beings, and the Imperishable among the perishable, sees indeed.

13.28.author: Swami Sivananda
13.28.text: He who sees the Supreme Lord existing truly in all beings, the imperishable within the perishable, sees indeed.

13.28.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.28.text: He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he is the one who truly sees.

13.29.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.29.text: Whoever, perceiving the Lord as abiding in all alike, does not harm themselves by themselves, they attain, on that account, the Supreme Goal.

13.29.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.29.text: For, seeing the ruler abiding alike in every place, he does not injure himself with his own mind and therefore reaches the highest goal.

13.29.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.29.text: Since, by truly seeing God, who is present everywhere alike, he does not injure the Self by the Self, he therefore attains the supreme Goal.

13.29.author: Swami Sivananda
13.29.text: For he who truly sees the same Lord dwelling everywhere does not destroy the Self by the self; rather, he attains the highest goal.

13.29.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.29.text: Beholding the Lord equally in all things, his actions do not mar his spiritual life but lead him to the heights of bliss.

13.30.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.30.text: Whoever views all actions as being performed (or all objects as being created) by the Material Cause itself, and at the same time views their own Self as a non-performer (or non-creator) - they view properly.

13.30.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.30.text: He who sees that all acts are done universally by Prakrti alone, and likewise that the self is not the doer, he indeed sees.

13.30.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.30.text: And he who sees actions being done in various ways by Nature itself, and also the Self as the non-agent, he sees.

13.30.author: Swami Sivananda
13.30.text: He sees, who sees that all actions are performed solely by Nature and that the Self is without action.

13.30.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.30.text: He who understands that it is only the Law of Nature that brings action to fruition, and that the Self never acts, alone knows the Truth.

13.31.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.31.text: When he perceives the mutual difference of beings as abiding in One, and its expansion from That alone, at that time he becomes the Brahman.

13.31.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.31.text: When he perceives the independent modes of existence of all beings centered in one, and their expansion from it alone, then he attains Brahman.

13.31.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.31.text: When one realizes that the state of diversity of living things is rooted in the One, and that their manifestation also comes from That, then one becomes identified with Brahman.

13.31.author: Swami Sivananda
13.31.text: When a person sees all beings as resting in the One and emanating from the One alone, they then become Brahman.

13.31.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.31.text: He who sees the diverse forms of life all rooted in One and growing forth from Him, shall indeed find the Absolute.

13.32.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.32.text: Because this is beginningless, and because this has no qualities, this Supreme Self is changeless and it neither acts nor gets stained [by actions], even though it dwells in the body, O son of Kunti!

13.32.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.32.text: This supreme Self, though dwelling in the body, is immutable, O Arjuna, being without beginning. It neither acts nor is tainted, as it is without Gunas.

13.32.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.32.text: Being without beginning and without end, O son of Kunti, this immutable, supreme Self does not act, nor is It affected [Also translated as tainted.-Tr.], although It exists in the body.

13.32.author: Swami Sivananda
13.32.text: Being without beginning, devoid of any qualities, the Supreme Self, imperishable, though dwelling in the body, O Arjuna, neither acts nor is tainted.

13.32.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.32.text: The Supreme Spirit, O Prince, is without beginning, has no qualities, and is imperishable. Though it is within the body, it does not act, nor is it affected by action.

13.33.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.33.text: Just as the all-pervasive Ether is not stained due to its subtlety, in the same way the Self, abiding in the body everywhere, is not stained.

13.33.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.33.text: As the all-pervading ether is not tainted due to its subtlety, even so, the self abiding in the body is not tainted everywhere.

13.33.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.33.text: As the all-pervading space is not defiled, due to its subtlety, similarly the Self, present everywhere in bodies, is not defiled.

13.33.author: Swami Sivananda
13.33.text: As the all-pervading ether is not tainted, due to its subtlety, so the Self seated everywhere in the body is not tainted either.

13.33.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.33.text: As space, though present everywhere, remains unaffected due to its subtlety, so too the Self, though present in all forms, retains its purity unalloyed.

13.34.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.34.text: Just as a single sun illuminates this entire world, so too does the Lord of the Field illuminate the entire Field, O descendant of Bharata!

13.34.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.34.text: As the one sun illuminates this entire world, so does the Knower of the Field (Ksetrin, the self), O Arjuna, illuminate the entire Field (the body).

13.34.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.34.text: As the single sun illuminates this entire world, similarly, O descendant of the Bharata dynasty, the Knower of the field illuminates the entire field.

13.34.author: Swami Sivananda
13.34.text: Just as the one sun illuminates the entire world, so too does the Lord of the field (Supreme Self) illuminate the entire field, O Arjuna.

13.34.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.34.text: As the one Sun illuminates the entire earth, so the Lord illuminates the entire universe.

13.35.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
13.35.text: Those who thus understand, with the knowledge-eye, the inner Soul of the Field and the Field-sensitizer, as well as the deliverance from the Material Cause of the elements—they attain the Supreme.

13.35.author: Swami Adidevananda
13.35.text: Those who thus discern, with the eye of knowledge, the difference between the body or the Field (Ksetra) and the knower of the body or Field-knower (Ksetrajna), and the means of deliverance from the manifested Prakrti, they attain the Supreme.

13.35.author: Swami Gambirananda
13.35.text: Those who, through the eye of wisdom, know the distinction between the field and the Knower of the field, and the annihilation of the Matrix of beings, reach the Supreme.

13.35.author: Swami Sivananda
13.35.text: They who, by the eye of knowledge, perceive the distinction between the field and its knower, as well as the liberation from the Nature of being, go to the Supreme.

13.35.author: Shri Purohit Swami
13.35.text: Those who, with the eyes of wisdom, thus see the difference between Matter and Spirit, and know how to liberate life from the Law of Nature, attain the Supreme.
